Post-deploy: the candidate demo is reached only through the restricted test listener/hostname -- zero public traffic, `candidatePublicTrafficPercent` 0, stable serving 100% -- and the walk is done in a real browser so a missing JS chunk shows up as a broken surface rather than as a green status code.
candidateVerificationJourney.notes: apiSideEffectsInScope is TRUE: ticking and editing on the candidate POSTs to #1713's endpoints and writes ledger rows for the Synthetic shop's own run. No vendor call, no production write. workersDisabledOnCandidate stays TRUE -- the endpoints are synchronous API writes, not worker tasks.

journeys.name: checklist-items-tracked-editable-and-non-gating
assertions: pre-merge: a run whose checklist endpoint returns items renders each item's TEXT and DONE STATE from the endpoint, and ticking one POSTS a tick for THAT ITEM'S ID -- asserted on the OUTBOUND REQUEST, not on component state (src/__tests__/run-checklist-items.test.tsx::items_render_from_the_endpoint_and_a_tick_posts_for_that_item)

pre-merge: a ticked item's tick AND its recorded time appear in the run view's ledger section, sourced from the run's own data; NO checklist state is held in `localStorage` -- asserted STRUCTURALLY over the module graph, so it cannot be reintroduced quietly later (ADR-094 d.5 names this drift class; #1320 deletes the mock that caused it) (src/__tests__/run-checklist-items.test.tsx::tick_and_its_time_appear_in_the_ledger_with_no_client_persistence)

pre-merge: editing an item's text POSTS the edit and renders THE TEXT THE SERVER RETURNED, not the text typed -- so a rejected or normalised edit is VISIBLE rather than silently kept (src/__tests__/run-checklist-items.test.tsx::an_edit_posts_and_renders_the_servers_returned_text)

pre-merge: with an item UN-ticked the run still advances a stage and NO control on the checklist surface blocks it -- asserted by scanning the rendered tree for a disabled-advance affordance (S-FR-12: ticks do not gate a run stage in v1; `ux-surface.md` F.5 option (b), never option (c)) (src/__tests__/run-checklist-items.test.tsx::checklist_does_not_gate_a_stage_advance)

pre-merge: the Thanh ly item (CE-FR-8) and the place-the-order item (RI-FR-4) each carry Juli's own disclaimer that it neither PERFORMS nor VERIFIES the step, in seller copy; EVERY seller-facing string this surface renders is collected from the RENDERED tree (not from a hand-listed constant array) and checked against `SELLER_COPY_BANNED_PATTERNS` imported from `packages/contracts/src/seller-copy.ts` -- the shared `packages/contracts/seller-copy-banned-patterns.json` source, never a local copy of the list (src/__tests__/run-checklist-items.test.tsx::disclaimers_render_and_seller_strings_pass_the_banned_pattern_guard)

pre-merge: every test input is a CAPTURED contract payload -- the golden fixtures in `packages/contracts/src/` and the tool-captured golden scenarios (#1311) -- driven through the real TypeScript contract types. Hand-authored event or envelope JSON is NOT an acceptable input (ADR-084 d.2); a shape the capture tool cannot yet produce is a gap in the tool, not a licence to type one out -- here specifically captured payloads from #1713's REAL endpoints

htmlRoutes: /decisions/recommendations/<concrete id whose plan carries checklist items>
staticAssetChecks.notes: The checklist components must be in the BUILT bundle on BOTH surfaces the seller meets them on -- the issue's own release-evidence line. A plan review that renders without its checklist section looks complete and is not. Route shapes verified against `apps/demo/src/app/` in this tree on 2026-09-08: the only page.tsx files under /decisions are `decisions/page.tsx`, `decisions/recommendations/[recommendationId]/page.tsx` and `decisions/in-progress/[executionId]/page.tsx`. There is NO `/decisions/in-progress` and NO `/decisions/recommendations` index route -- the In-Progress view is the SAME HTML document at /decisions under the `?tab=in-progress` query param (`recommendations-view.tsx` reads `searchParams.get("tab")`). Earlier plans (#1314, #1318) named those two as routes; probing them as HTML routes would 404 and the probe must not be written that way.

migrationCompatibility.notes: NO SCHEMA CHANGE. The checklist tables are #1712's and the tick / untick / edit endpoints with their ledger rows are #1713's; both are hard dependencies of this slice. This slice's whole diff is under `apps/demo/**` and `packages/contracts/src/**`; it opens no migration file, and the migration numbers for the backend slices it depends on are RESERVED BY META and never read from head. If a test cannot pass without a column or an endpoint, the dependency is unmet and the answer is to stop and report, not to write a migration or a second route. Stable and candidate are compatible because the previous bundle simply does not render the new surface, and the rows and routes it reads are unchanged by this slice.

rollbackAssertion.preCutoverFailureBehavior: Do not merge; discard the candidate and keep the retained previous bundle serving 100%. There is no checklist concept on the client today, so nothing is stranded.
rollbackAssertion.postCutoverFailureBehavior: Redeploy the retained previous demo bundle. Additive on the client: reverting leaves the items UNRENDERED and the server rows INTACT -- no tick is lost, because no tick was ever held client-side. Assert on the rolled-back bundle that the plan review and run view still render and are not half-wired to a checklist section that no longer exists.
rollbackAssertion.notes: The PREVIOUS demo bundle is RETAINED and stays serving 100% of public traffic until the candidate passes; rollback is redeploying that retained bundle. Rollback is NOT automatic for this slice: the failure modes here are visual and structural (a surface that renders blank, a chunk that 404s), which a health probe does not catch, so a human reads the candidate journey and decides. No schema step is involved in either direction.

doNotInfer: Do NOT add a surface. v1's seller surfaces are the seven S-FR-1 names -- card, plan review, confirmation sheet, run view, completion message + exception list, notification centre, deadline list -- plus the single deadline view added by the owner waiver of 2026-09-05 (#1790, and ONLY #1790). A slice that believes it needs an eighth surface, a new tab, a new modal shell or a new route is a signal the routing or the design is wrong: STOP AND REPORT, do not build it.

Do NOT hand-author event or envelope JSON, anywhere, for any reason. ADR-084 d.2 forbids it: a second hand-maintained source drifts from the first while both suites stay green -- the defect class behind six W3 post-merge fixes. Test inputs are the captured contract payloads and the tool-captured golden scenarios (#1311). ADR-094 d.5 relaxes this ONLY for the existing client replay in `mock-data.ts`, which this slice neither extends nor imitates.

Do NOT write English seller-facing copy. Vietnamese only, second person ("ban"), per S-NFR-4 and S-NFR-12; there is no EN toggle in v1 (`ux-surface.md` F.12 option (a)). An English label, an English empty state, an English error, or an English tooltip is a defect even when it never ships to a Vietnamese seller in the demo walk.

Do NOT let an internal identifier reach seller-facing text. No `workflow_key`, tool name, playbook key, predicate or guard name, stop-reason identifier, `subject_ref`, run id, order id, SKU id or warehouse id in any rendered string (ADR-084 d.5, S-NFR-4). The banned-pattern guard is the floor, not the ceiling: an identifier the regex list happens not to match is still a defect.

Do NOT read the workflow's identity from anything but the seller-facing envelope. Grouping, gating and labelling derive from `recommendation.workflow_name` and the `is_executable` discriminator that `packages/contracts/src/decisions.ts` already carries; `workflow_key` is absent from that envelope by ADR-084 d.3 and must NOT be reintroduced, inferred, reverse-engineered from a title, or smuggled in through a URL segment. If a v1 workflow cannot be distinguished without leaking the taxonomy, STOP AND REPORT (#1793).

Do NOT render a value outside a numeric field's validated range, and do NOT invent the range. Bounds come from the contract descriptor (`packages/contracts/src/review.ts`), never from a component literal; CE-FR-4's stock goal is `0 <= goal < sellable` and RI-NFR-3 forbids a write below the committed quantity. A control that can express an out-of-range value -- an unclamped slider, a free-text number, a spinner without bounds -- is the defect, whether or not a validator catches it afterwards (#1783).

Do NOT change a backend route, response model, payload producer or database row from this slice. Domain is ui-ux, one domain per issue; the producers are named in the issue's Blocked-by list. Do NOT open `apps/dashboard/`, `ios/`, `backend/src/juli_backend/ai/`, `backend/src/juli_backend/workers/` or the TikTok corpora catalogs (ADR-051) -- this epic's doNotLoad list.

Do NOT prove a contract with a `**kwargs` double or a hand-rolled stub of a contract type. Bind every test collaborator to the REAL exported type and the REAL module; a double proves routing, never that the real payload would render. Consumer-without-producer is the failure this wave exists to prevent.

Do NOT hold checklist text or done state in `localStorage`, a React ref, a module-level cache, or any other client-side mutable copy. There is ONE source: #1713's endpoint. This is the exact drift ADR-094 d.5 names and #1320 deletes.

Do NOT add gating. An un-ticked item never blocks a stage advance in v1, and this surface must contain NO control that could make it look as though it does -- not a disabled button, not a warning, not a progress bar that stalls.
Do NOT render the text the seller typed after an edit. Render what the server RETURNED, so a normalisation or a rejection is visible.
Do NOT add server behaviour. The endpoints, the ledger rows and the no-gating rule are #1713's; if an endpoint is missing, the dependency is unmet -- stop and report.
